articles.title: We planned one day in Jagdalpur and ended up staying three
articles.deck: Six of us went from Hyderabad with a youth event in mind. A hundred young people came, the hall ran out of floor, and children sat on the stage so that more adults could stand.

archiveMeta.editNote: First published across pages 16 to 19 of the January-February 2017 issue as "AWAKE Mission Trip 2016", by the author. Copy-edited for grammar, tense and punctuation only; no sentence has been added and nothing has been reworded beyond what the grammar required. Two changes of substance, both subtractions. The names of the host church in Jagdalpur, its pastor and his wife, and its two youth leaders are withheld: Chhattisgarh has an anti-conversion statute, and a named public record of a local congregation hosting an outreach carries a risk for them that it did not carry for a webzine in 2017. They can be restored at any time if they ask. The 2017 page also reported how many young people rededicated their lives during the conference; that figure is omitted here for the same reason. Pages 17 and 18 of the original are photographs.

body.v: Written in 2017, about a trip made in 2016. The names of the host church in Jagdalpur and of its pastors and youth leaders are withheld here, at the magazine's decision and not theirs.
The mission trip to Jagdalpur was initially planned as a one-day youth event, but it was God's plan for it to be three: two days of youth conference, and three evenings of gospel outreach meetings.

A team of six went to Jagdalpur from Sharon Church, Hyderabad. My wife Deepakshi and I, with our two-year-old, Arlene. Elizabeth Clayton on keyboard and vocals. Praveen on drums. Esther and Karuna on choir and choreography.

The three days were absolutely astounding and I am still amazed at the work of God and his goodness. We felt the movement of the Holy Spirit during the youth conference. About a hundred young people took part. I focused on two topics: on the first day “You are God's masterpiece”, and on the second “Discover your talents for the Kingdom of God”. I encouraged them with the testimony of how my life was transformed. They were eager to listen to the word of God.

We divided the young people into groups according to the talents they shared, and gave each group time to present on the topic. We watched a Christian song composed in a tribal language, and they danced to it in the tribal tune and music. We worshipped, danced and praised Jesus, and met his goodness.

Deepakshi shared about the salvation wristband, explaining the meaning of the coloured beads on it. It was an effective tool for sharing the good news with friends. They were excited about it, and the idea was new for them.

Elizabeth Clayton led the worship during the altar call and the worship session with the team. People were moved by the music and the song. Praveen was rocking with the electronic drum pad. Many testified that during the worship they felt heaven, and had goosebumps.

Even in the first evening meeting God spoke to his people powerfully. I gave an illustrated sermon on the life of David, with epic background music. The message was on how David was favoured by God in his teenage years, while he was experiencing frustration from his brothers. It was one hour, power-packed, with a dramatic message, and the crowd felt as though they had gone back to David's time. Literally half the group who came forward for prayer were knocked off their feet under God's power.

On the second day it just grew. I spoke on the spiritual blessings, quoting Ephesians 1:3-9, and on the story of the crippled Mephibosheth — how King David showed him favour, remembering the promise he had made with his friend Jonathan. People were enjoying the story in spirit and praying for spiritual blessings.

The third day was a Sunday. More people came rushing into the hall. There was no space; children had to sit on the stage to make room for others. Mostly it was non-believers coming in. I focused on miracles through faith, from the story of blind Bartimaeus. God came with his amazing glory. People were filled with the Holy Spirit, crying out to God, worshipping, and experiencing miracles and healing. God is moving over the people in Jagdalpur for revival. We marvelled at God's mercy towards us all, and at how deeply he loves us.

We got connected with the pastor of a local church and his wife. They are truly an inspiration to us, and I am amazed at their dedication to the growth of the church and at the positive impact they have as leaders. We also met their two youth leaders, who lead the worship team. We had an amazing time with them, in the church and exploring the beauty of nature nearby, visiting the waterfalls.

We would like to thank you all, our well-wishers and friends, who prayed and supported us for the success of the conference. All I wanted to share with you is that this event was so blessed, and beyond our imagination. Such an amazing experience. We learned many things from the local church. We give all glory and praise to God for choosing us for this mission trip.
